minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted David Butler an extension of his expired special permit to rebuild the house at 56 Pine Street.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard David Butler's request to reinstate a 2020 special permit, expired after he demolished the old house, to rebuild a single-family home at 56 Pine Street. Board members asked about the wells and about transferring the permit to a buyer. They granted the extension with standard conditions and then adjourned.

votes.motion: Grant the extension of the special permit for 56 Pine Street.

decisions.decision: Special permit extension granted, conditioned on compliance with all applicable laws and subject to periodic review; it must be recorded at the registry of deeds, and lapses within 2 years unless construction has substantially begun.
Board members indicated the permit is granted to the applicant personally, so a buyer would have to reapply and appear before the board, though the lot is buildable.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted to pass an extension of David Butler's expired special permit to rebuild a single-family house at 56 Pine Street.
The extension carries conditions: compliance with applicable laws, periodic review, and recording at the registry of deeds.
The permit lapses within two years unless construction has substantially begun.
Board members indicated the permit is granted to the applicant personally, so a buyer would have to reapply and appear before the board, though the lot is buildable.

why_it_matters: The two-year limit and the personal nature of the permit mean the rebuild must start on a clock, and a sale of the lot would send a new owner back to the board for fresh approval.
watch_next: Whether construction substantially begins within two years of the grant, or the permit lapses.
